extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and respondents in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) proceedings; USPTO staff and legal professionals handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order imposing exclusion from practice before the USPTO under the reciprocal-discipline regulation 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-bar discipline, describing required responses, procedural service, sanctions, and administrative steps for exclusion and possible reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline standard under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), if there is no genuine issue of material fact the Director may impose reciprocal discipline (here, exclusion) identical to that imposed by a State disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that to contest imposition of exclusion under § 11.24(d) he must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information he believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that identical discipline would be unwarranted under the grounds permissible in § 11.24(d)(1). The Final Order determined there was no genuine issue and imposed exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response requirement to Notice and Order (40-day rule and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must file a response within 40 days to contest reciprocal discipline and must include all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice was mailed first-class certified mail (return receipt requested) to known addresses; where mailings were returned/unclaimed, service by publication was used. The response requirement is jurisdictional to create a contested factual record under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (mailing, forwarding, and publication) under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When mailings to provided addresses are returned or unclaimed, the Office may effect service by publication in the Official Gazette per 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed to addresses provided by Respondent; returned mail and forwarding notices were documented; service by publication was published in the Official Gazette (dates provided) and the publication advised how Respondent could obtain a copy by written request to the USPTO General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline was imposed for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by consenting to have his name stricken from the roll of attorneys licensed to practice in Virginia while disciplinary charges were pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains the State Bar accepted Respondent's consent to revocation while charges were pending and that Respondent admitted the material facts upon which allegations of misconduct were predicated; such admissions and consenting to striking of name when charges pending supports reciprocal discipline under the cited rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct supporting discipline (financial and client-related failures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged misconduct included: sending USPTO electronic fund transfers aggregating $37,170 that were denied for insufficient funds; sending checks to the USPTO aggregating $110,875 that were returned unpaid for insufficient funds; failing to keep clients fully and timely informed of application status and adverse effects from inability to advance fees; failing to apply costs advanced by a business entity in Taiwan to the pertinent applications and using those funds for other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific factual allegations are cited as the basis for the State Bar discipline and thus as supporting reciprocal discipline by the USPTO; financial irresponsibility, failure to communicate with clients, and misuse/misapplication of client-advanced funds are highlighted as culpable conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies ancillary measures tied to exclusion (see compliance with §11.58, limited recognition for 30 days to facilitate compliance, dissociation of customer numbers and PKI, prohibitions on use/obtaining customer numbers or PKI until reinstated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order grants limited recognition to practice for 30 days solely to facilitate Respondent's compliance with § 11.58(b). The text does not reproduce § 11.58 but makes compliance a condition of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating compliance with § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow, time-limited authorization intended only to permit the excluded practitioner to take steps required by § 11.58 (e.g., client notifications or transfer of files) within the 30-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate the Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate, nor obtain a USPTO customer number or PKI certificate, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Notice of Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion (text provided) in the Official Gazette and post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion summarizes the charges, factual allegations, regulatory basis for discipline, and references statutory authority; disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room URL provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the OED Director to provide such notice as part of the administrative consequences of public discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 in connection with any request for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires adherence to the reinstatement regulation; the Final Order does not restate the content of § 11.60 but makes compliance a condition for consideration of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority cited for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly anchors the USPTO's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish/notify under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice includes a specific URL for the OED Reading Room and states that the OED Director shall publish the Final Order and Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette; publication dates for the service-by-publication are shown as examples.
